title: Prevent RSV lower respiratory tract disease in older adults through vaccination

concept.text: Prevent clinically important RSV respiratory disease in older adults using active immunization. This achieved target is distinct from infant monoclonal-antibody prophylaxis and from universal respiratory vaccines. Proposed completion test: FDA vaccine licensure for adults aged at least 60 years, supported by a randomized trial of more than 20,000 participants showing efficacy against laboratory-confirmed RSV lower respiratory tract disease during the first season. Test set by: FDA; the Arexvy clinical programme and regulatory review supply the population and endpoint. Reported achieved: FDA approved Arexvy on 3 May 2023. Overlaps: VIR-04. Sources given: [FDA first RSV vaccine announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-vaccine) ; [FDA Arexvy regulatory assessment](https://www.fda.gov/media/168519/download).

page.title: RSV vaccines against lower respiratory tract disease in older adults
page.definition: Vaccination reduces laboratory-confirmed lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD), which affects the lungs and lower airways, caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in adults aged 60 years or older.

goal.need: ACIP’s 2023 review quantified annual US RSV hospitalizations and deaths among adults aged ≥65 years, shown below. Vaccination targets the lower respiratory tract disease contributing to this burden. ACIP noted that undertesting and limited diagnostic sensitivity affect burden estimates.

figures.caption: Annual US RSV burden among adults aged ≥65 years, estimated in ACIP’s 2023 review.
figures.note: These are burden estimates reported before routine adult RSV vaccination.

statements.body: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices
statements.quote: RSV vaccination might prevent substantial morbidity in older adults at risk for severe RSV disease
Today’s approval of the first RSV vaccine is an important public health achievement to prevent a disease which can be life-threatening
statements.context: Peter Marks, director of FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, discussing the first RSV vaccine approval.

completion.title: FDA licenses a vaccine against RSV lower respiratory tract disease in adults aged ≥60 years.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a biologics license application for a vaccine indicated for active immunization to prevent lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) caused by RSV in individuals 60 years of age and older. The licence rests on a randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in adults aged ≥60 years (25,040 randomized in the trial behind the first such licence) in which efficacy against a first episode of RT-PCR-confirmed RSV LRTD in the first RSV season met its prespecified success criterion, a lower confidence limit above 20%. Efficacy in later seasons, against hospitalization or death, and in adults under 60 is not required. Antibody products and vaccines given to protect infants do not count.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration: Arexvy biologics license approval letter, 3 May 2023, and Summary Basis for Regulatory Action.
completion.threshold_quote: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine, Adjuvanted is indicated for active immunization for the prevention of lower respiratory tract disease caused by respiratory syncytial virus in individuals 60 years of age and older.
completion.basis: A first: FDA described Arexvy on 3 May 2023 as “the first respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine approved for use in the United States”. The licence fixes the indication and population. Its pivotal trial, AReSVi-006, randomized 25,040 adults; efficacy against RSV LRTD was 82.6% (96.95% CI 57.9–94.1) over a median 6.7 months, against a success criterion of a lower limit above 20%. The endpoint and criterion are those FDA accepted for this trial (milestone m3), not an Atlas threshold. FDA required postmarketing studies of Guillain–Barré syndrome and acute disseminated encephalomyelitis.

milestones.title: An RSV vaccine passes FDA’s preclinical assessment for testing in people.
milestones.criterion: Laboratory, animal and product-quality evidence supports FDA’s determination that human testing is reasonably safe under an investigational new drug application. For Arexvy, FDA reviewed two repeat-dose rabbit toxicity studies of RSVPreF3 antigen alone or combined with AS01B, a related adjuvant, alongside studies of the AS01E adjuvant components. FDA’s assessment dated 3 May 2023 identified no significant nonclinical safety issues.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Vaccine Development – 101, preclinical testing and investigational new drug assessment.
milestones.threshold_quote: reasonably safe for testing of the vaccine to move forward in people.

milestones.title: An RSV vaccine passes the safety reviews required to continue a phase 1/2 trial.
milestones.criterion: Independent data monitoring committee reviews after vaccination permit continuation of the registered phase 1/2 study NCT03814590. The randomized study enrolled 48 adults aged 18–40 years and 1,005 adults aged 60–80 years across vaccine and placebo groups, using two doses two months apart. It ended on 23 February 2021. The committee identified no safety concerns precluding any tested formulation; safety and immune-response results supported selecting a formulation for further development.
milestones.set_by: GSK, registered study NCT03814590; required independent safety reviews described in the peer-reviewed phase 1/2 report.
milestones.threshold_quote: IDMC evaluations identified no safety concerns precluding use of any vaccine formulation throughout the study.

milestones.title: RSV vaccine efficacy against LRTD at age ≥60 has a lower 96.95% confidence bound above 20%.
milestones.criterion: In adults aged ≥60 years, the lower bound of the two-sided 96.95% confidence interval for efficacy against first-season, externally adjudicated, RT-PCR-confirmed RSV LRTD must exceed 20%, counting cases from day 15. LRTD requires ≥2 lower respiratory symptoms/signs including ≥1 sign, or ≥3 lower respiratory symptoms, lasting ≥24 hours. At 11 April 2022, AReSVi-006 reported 7/12,466 vaccine versus 40/12,494 placebo cases: efficacy 82.6% (96.95% CI 57.9%–94.1%), median follow-up 6.7 months.
milestones.set_by: GSK, AReSVi-006 registered protocol NCT04886596, primary efficacy success criterion reported in the trial publication.
milestones.threshold_quote: a lower limit of the confidence interval around the efficacy estimate of more than 20%.

milestones.title: FDA’s review committee recommends approval of an RSV vaccine for adults aged ≥60 years.
milestones.criterion: FDA’s multidisciplinary review concludes that clinical, nonclinical and product-related evidence supports approval for prevention of RSV LRTD in adults aged ≥60 years. On 3 May 2023, the Arexvy review committee recommended approval for the labeled indication after judging the benefits greater than the risks. The review required postmarketing studies addressing Guillain–Barré syndrome and acute disseminated encephalomyelitis.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Arexvy Summary Basis for Regulatory Action, recommended regulatory action and benefit/risk assessment.
milestones.threshold_quote: The Review Committee recommends approval of this product.

not_found: No universal numerical preclinical or phase 1/2 pass threshold was found in FDA development guidance or the published RSVPreF3 phase 1/2 report.
The public FDA summary does not disclose rabbit sample sizes for the two repeat-dose toxicity studies.

results.finding: FDA's Arexvy assessment included 2 repeat-dose rabbit toxicity studies; animal sample sizes were not reported, and no significant nonclinical safety issues were identified.
results.detail: The report establishes a favorable nonclinical assessment during BLA review, but does not explicitly report FDA's determination that human testing could proceed under the IND.
results.quote: CBER concluded that there are no significant safety issues.

results.finding: Study 002 reported acceptable reactogenicity and supported formulation selection; the listed relevant older-adult groups comprised 100 vaccine and 101 placebo recipients.
results.detail: Safety and immunogenicity supported further development, but the source does not report independent monitoring committee decisions permitting trial continuation or the full trial enrollment specified in the criterion.
results.quote:
Both adjuvanted formulations had acceptable
reactogenicity profile.

results.finding: Arexvy in adults ≥60 years (12,466 vaccine; 12,494 placebo) achieved a 96.95% confidence lower bound of 57.9% for efficacy against first-season RSV LRTD.
results.detail: Externally adjudicated, RT-PCR-confirmed cases were counted from day 15 through April 11, 2022; median follow-up was 6.7 months. The lower confidence bound exceeded 20%.
results.quote:
The case split was 7 cases in the RSVPreF3-AS01E group 
compared to 40 cases in the placebo group with a VE of 82.6% (96.95% CI 57.9, 
94.1).

results.finding: FDA's review committee recommended Arexvy approval for adults ≥60 years, supported by a pivotal trial with 25,040 randomized participants.
results.detail: The May 3, 2023 multidisciplinary review found benefits greater than risks and required postmarketing studies addressing Guillain–Barré syndrome and acute disseminated encephalomyelitis.
results.quote:
the Review Committee recommends approval of
AREXVY for the labeled indication and usage.

results.finding: RSVPreF3 vaccines in 48 young and 1,005 older adults: IDMC reviews found 0 safety concerns precluding use of any formulation.
results.detail: NCT03814590 required IDMC safety reviews after vaccination for continuation. Participants received two doses two months apart; the study ended 23 February 2021. Safety and immunogenicity supported selecting a formulation for further development.
results.quote:
IDMC evaluations identified no safety concerns precluding use 
of any vaccine formulation throughout the study.

results.finding: RSVPreF3 OA in 24,960 adults aged ≥60: the lower 96.95% confidence bound for first-season RSV LRTD efficacy was 57.9%, exceeding 20%.
results.detail: Externally adjudicated, RT-PCR-confirmed LRTD counted from day 15 using the specified symptom/sign definition. There were 7/12,466 vaccine versus 40/12,494 placebo cases through April 11, 2022; median follow-up was 6.7 months.
results.quote:
The vaccine efficacy was 
82.6% (96.95% confidence interval [CI], 57.9 to 
94.1) (Table 2); thus, the primary objective was 
met (lower limit of confidence interval, >20%).

results.finding: FDA licensed AREXVY to prevent RSV LRTD in adults aged ≥60 years; trial sample size is not reported in this letter.
results.detail: Approval effective May 3, 2023. This replacement letter corrects the adjuvant dating period and preserves the original approval date.
results.quote:
We have approved your BLA for Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine, Adjuvanted 
effective this date.

results.finding: RSVPreF3 phase 1/2 trial in 48 young and 1,005 older adults: IDMC reviews identified 0 safety concerns precluding use of any formulation.
results.detail: NCT03814590 required IDMC safety reviews after vaccination for study continuation. Two doses were given two months apart; the study ended on 23 February 2021. Safety and immunogenicity supported selection of the 120-AS01E formulation.
results.quote:
IDMC evaluations identified no safety concerns precluding use 
of any vaccine formulation throughout the study.

results.finding: RV-1770 received FDA IND clearance in December 2023 for human testing; planned Phase I enrollment was 162 participants.
results.detail: The planned trial includes adults aged 60–79. The filing reports completed FDA IND clearance but does not describe the underlying nonclinical safety assessment; the enrollment figure is planned, not observed.
results.quote:
In December 2023, RNAimmune received regulatory clearance on its IND application 
from the U.S. FDA to commence a Phase I clinical trial for RV-1770, an mRNA vaccine 
targeting the human RSV.

results.finding: SCB-1019 received FDA IND clearance for a revaccination trial planned to enroll up to 160 adults aged 60–85.
results.detail: The filing reports FDA clearance for human testing. It does not describe the underlying nonclinical studies; 160 is planned clinical enrollment, not a preclinical sample size.

The Company is pleased to announce Investigational New Drug (IND) clearance by the United
